source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Gather data from air quality monitoring stations and sensors near the industrial facility. This may include hourly, daily, or real-time information on pollutant levels and meteorological data.
3. Log pollutant concentrations for significant harmful emissions such as sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), particulate matter (PM10, PM2.5), carbon monoxide (CO), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and any specific hazardous air pollutants (HAPs) relevant to the industry in question.
4. Record dates, times, sampling methods, and instrument calibrations used to ensure the accuracy and credibility of the data.
5. Highlight anomalies or exceedances of applicable regulatory thresholds (such as National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) in the US or equivalent local standards).
6. Keep maintenance records and quality assurance/quality control information for all monitoring equipment used.

7. Use modeling and estimation techniques.
8. If direct monitoring
